result:
All 14 queries ran and returned sensible answers. I checked T12 and T13 by hand against the CSV, and both matched. I didn't hand-check the rest.

Two choices in the queries:
- **T8:** the pair is named with `:p /` so `/1` can still be read after `/0` has changed the subject.
- **T12/T13:** `parseJson` turns the CSV text into numbers.

T1: /data/users | filter ~(/active | eq true) | filter ~(/email | ne null) | filter ~(/email | lower | endsWith "@example.com") | count
T2: /data/users | filter ~(/roles | map ~(lower) | contains "admin") | map ~(/name) | sort ~(lower)
T3: /data/users | map ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :country | coalesce "unknown") | groupBy ~(/) | map ~(count)
T4: /data/users | map ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2
T5: filter ~(/state | eq "open") | map ~(/labels | map ~(/name | lower)) | flat | distinct | sort
T6: sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 | map ~({:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | coalesce null | at :login | coalesce null)})
T7: filter ~(/state | eq "open") | map ~(at :assignee | coalesce null) | filter ~(ne null) | map ~(/login) | groupBy ~(/) | map ~(count)
T8: :r / | /dependencies | union (r | /devDependencies) | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) | map ~(:p / | /0 | keyword | append "@" | append (p | /1))
T9: /services | filter ~(at :enabled | coalesce false | eq true) | filter ~(/port | gt 8000) | map ~(/name | lower) | sort | join ","
T10: lines | map ~(split " ") | filter ~(/1 | eq "ERROR") | groupBy ~(/2) | map ~(count)
T11: lines | filter ~(contains "ms=") | map ~(split " " | filter ~(startsWith "ms=") | first | drop 3 | parseJson) | avg | round 1
T12: lines | drop 1 | filter ~(ne "") | map ~(split ",") | filter ~(/5 | lower | eq "shipped") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | map ~({:q (/3 | parseJson) :p (/4 | parseJson)} | mulOf /q /p) | sum | round 2
T13: lines | drop 1 | filter ~(ne "") | map ~(split ",") | filter ~(/5 | lower | ne "cancelled") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | map ~({:c /1 :t ({:q (/3 | parseJson) :p (/4 | parseJson)} | mulOf /q /p)}) | groupBy ~(/c) | map ~(map ~(/t) | sum | round 2) | entries | sort ~(/1 | desc) | take 2 | map ~({:customer (/0 | keyword) :total /1})
